title: Concept: File access built from input (shell) — review required
description: In shell, cat $f assembles a filesystem path from parts. Traversal payloads (..%2f, absolute paths, symlink races) redirect the operation outside its directory. The shell-specific remedy is confinement via a case-allowlist of file names.
applicability: shell codebases opening files with assembled paths; single-line lexical scope.
risk: Arbitrary file read or write when untrusted input reaches the path; HIGH severity because traversal payloads are trivial and impact is filesystem-wide.
